accuracy.evidence: Checked against NC 2013 Y2 measurement (money): 'recognise and use symbols for pounds (£) and pence (p); combine amounts to make a particular value'; 'find different combinations of coins that equal the same amounts of money'; 'solve simple problems in a practical context involving addition and subtraction of money of the same unit, including giving change'; and Y3 'add and subtract amounts of money to give change, using both £ and p'. UK coin set 1p-£2 with 7-sided 20p and 50p and a 12-sided £1 (Royal Mint). Lab arithmetic checked: 47 = 20+20+5+2; 100-63 = 37 via 63+5+2+10+20; £1.45+£0.80 = £2.25, £5-£2.25 = £2.75; 37p in 4 coins is the minimum (3 coins reach at most 20+10+5 = 35p below 37 without a 2p). Parameterised items checked at corners: p2 100-c 11..89, p3 a+b 35..95, m2 10t+5f 15..80, m6 100-2p 10..70.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets documented early money errors (NCETM Y2 money guidance; White Rose Y2/Y3 small steps): more coins means more money (step 1 prediction, tags count/same, p1, m3); £/p mixing such as £1.45 + 80p = £81.45 (BARWHY, tag units, m4) and 80p read as 8p (tag eight); the 100 − 63 = 47 exchange slip (step 3 prediction, tag borrow); adding when change is asked (tags add/plus, the bar model rejects the change card in the cost box and vice versa); and many small coins instead of fewest (step 5 feedback for 37p with 5+ coins, tags big/ones, p5).

lab_distinct.evidence: flagcoin is built around coin value and change: a drag-to-purse coin tray that judges exact payment, a detector for genuinely different coin sets (same coins re-ordered are rejected), counting up on an open number line for change, a two-step bar model with a cost box and a change box, and a fewest-coins greedy task. flagbudget (teen budgeting) and flagnline (placing numbers) share none of these mechanics. Max 6-shingle similarity 3.6% (with flag_vib.js).

lab_teaches.evidence: The learner finds the rule by acting: over-paying shows '(too much)' and the amount over; a second set of coins for 20p is accepted only if the coins differ, which surfaces 'same value, different coins'; the number line refuses jumps past £1 and prompts 'jump to the next ten first'; the cost box only takes the sum and the narration names it as the total, not the answer yet; a 6-coin 37p gets 'can you use bigger coins?'.

predictions.evidence: Three predictions with tempting wrong options: who has more money, 6 coins or 2 ('Ben: more coins'; the purse shows value, not count); change from £1 for 63p ('47p', the exchange slip; the jumps add to 37p); first step to find change ('take 80p from £5'; the bar model needs the total first).

challenge_feedback.evidence: Twelve distinct messages in why(): count, same, ten, one, borrow, add, units, eight, plus, slip, big, ones, each naming the error (e.g. '80p is £0.80, not £80'; 'Two 10p coins can be one 20p'). Steps add their own: over-pay message with the amount, duplicate-way message, past-£1 jump message, per-card bar-model messages (BARWHY) and the total-vs-change swap messages.

readability.evidence: validate_lessons passes for the family audience. Kid text uses sentences of 5-14 words and plain words (value, total cost, change, count up); £ and p are introduced with 100p = £1. Coin faces show 1p-£2 in bold dark text on pale coin colours; buttons are '+ 20p', '+5p', 'Take one out', and the number-line labels are 11-13 px.

no_filler.evidence: Content gate passes (explanation overlap 0.3% at most). Kid paragraphs: value not count; £ and p and ways to make 20p; total cost; change by counting up. Adult paragraphs: Y2/Y3 statements and key words; named mistakes; why counting up and bar models; what the lab does.

mobile.evidence: Screenshots before and after Show me at 360 px Android (light and dark). First pass ran the second tray row off the canvas, spaced purse coins to the purse edges, overlapped the found-ways list with the tray and put the bar-model cards below the canvas edge; fixed with a smaller narrow tray at 68% height, fixed coin spacing in the purse, found ways listed inside the empty purse, and cards raised to 70%. Coins are 25-30 px radius tap targets; bar cards 48+ px tall.

accessibility.evidence: Every canvas action has a labelled button: 'Put a 20p coin in the purse', 'Take the last coin out of the purse', 'Jump on 5 pence', 'Undo the last jump', 'Put £2.25 in the cost box'. report() updates the canvas aria-label and narration after each action with the running total. walk.cjs: desktop and iPhone 13 complete all 5 tasks with Show me, the challenge shows, axe clean in both themes, no console errors.
